rows.subtype: Approach: keeps closing the nearest gap and never steps back to check the route [Pitfall]
rows.description: A student repeatedly fixes the loudest problem in a project, such as a bug, then a slide, then a formatting issue, and drifts away from the main requirement until the deadline.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Approach: notices a dead end and sets a temporary detour subgoal [Revision]
rows.description: An engineer stuck because a needed library will not install pauses, sets a subgoal of testing in a container, and returns to the original gap once the environment works.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Approach: tries the same action in different ways until something works [Action]
rows.description: A toddler tries to fit a round block into a square hole, turns it, presses harder, then moves to the round hole and it drops in. The success teaches without any words.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Approach: tests several options and remembers which worked [Thinking]
rows.description: A child building a paper boat tries folding it three ways and floats each in a bucket. The one with a wider base stays upright, so she folds that one from then on.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Approach: makes small changes one at a time and watches the result [Action]
rows.description: A boy tuning his kite changes the tail length, then the string position. Because he alters one thing per flight, he learns that the longer tail steadies it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Approach: random changes with no record of what was tried [Pitfall]
rows.description: A teenager fixing a phone's slow Wi-Fi flips settings at random, forgets which he changed, and ends up worse off. Without notes, error gives no reliable learning.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Approach: switches to noting each attempt and its outcome [Revision]
rows.description: A student debugging code after a night of random edits starts a log of what he changed and what happened, and finds the fault within twenty minutes.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Approach: uses safe cheap trials when testing is inexpensive and mistakes are recoverable [Thinking]
rows.description: A new cook adjusts spices across several small pots of dal rather than one big batch. Cheap, reversible trials let her explore quickly without wasting much.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Approach: picks the first option that is good enough and stops looking [Thinking]
rows.description: A girl needs a cover for her notebook and takes the first plain one that fits and is not torn, instead of checking every shelf at the stationery shop.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Approach: sets a minimum standard in advance and chooses the first option that meets it [Action]
rows.description: A teenager choosing a study spot decides it must be quiet, have a table and be within ten minutes. The second place he checks meets all three, so he takes it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
